title: H^1 of a sheaf classifies extensions of the structure sheaf by it
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-cohomology.tex (Cohomology on Sites), section on extensions of sheaves and H^1
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file sites-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts a canonical bijection between Ext^1_{Mod(O)}(O, F) and H^1(C, F) which sends an extension 0 -> F -> E -> O -> 0 to the image of 1 in Gamma(C, O) under the connecting map (statement lines 374-386). The proof does not verify the map but constructs its inverse: an injective embedding F contained in I with Q = I/F is chosen, the long exact cohomology sequence identifies the given class with a global section of Q, and that section is used as the map along which the extension 0 -> F -> I -> Q -> 0 is pulled back (proof lines 390-413). What makes this non-formal is that the two directions must be compared through the same connecting map, which is why an injective resolution rather than an arbitrary resolution is used, and the pullback must be organised as a map of short exact sequences to produce the extension. The claim is H2: the construction is short and ends by citing the standard theory of extensions.
